What will count toward my degree?

Compare a course against the exact degree requirement it can fill. The receiving school, program, course version, credit amount and academic level matter. A familiar subject title or an inexpensive offer does not establish a usable placement. Grades, exam scores, recommendation dates and duplicate-credit rules also belong in the match.

ACE and NCCRS recommend credit; they do not turn a course provider into an accredited degree-granting college. Credit exams, recommended courses and university-issued credit may follow different rules at the same destination. Start from the researched course choices in your plan instead of assembling a provider list first.

Can I study at my own pace without a proctored exam?

Compare pace and assessment separately. Sophia describes self-paced study with a limit on active courses; written or project work can affect completion time. The Study.com college-credit guidance cited below describes open-book, non-proctored finals, while its course-specific work and membership choice still matter. StraighterLine’s cited final Benchmark instructions require Honorlock.

Self-paced does not mean proctor-free. Use the pace and assessment labels to find a format you can realistically finish. Compare the exact credit-earning product, assignments and assessment arrangements rather than assuming every product from one provider works the same way.

When would an exam be a good choice?

CLEP and DSST can suit a subject you already know or can prepare for efficiently. The school’s exam policy determines the required score, course award and degree placement. Exams remain one option alongside coursework; a passing score does not establish which requirement it fills.

Modern States provides CLEP preparation and eligible exam vouchers. The preparation is not extra credit on top of the CLEP result. Saylor Direct Credit requires its designated credit assessment, not an ordinary completion certificate; include its proctoring requirements in your comparison. Voucher eligibility, testing charges and record fees can also affect the total.

What if my school needs another kind of credit?

Institutional courses can be useful where a school’s policy calls for college-issued credit. ASU Universal Learner Courses offers a process for eligible learners to complete a course and purchase ASU credit. TEL-delivered courses involve a selected partner institution and eligibility conditions. Preserve the original source and credit-granting institution; a different transcript does not automatically remove a destination’s source restrictions.

Coopersmith and Davar offer designated NCCRS-recommended learning that can suit particular remaining subjects where permitted. Compare the exact placement, access rules, books, assignments and proctor arrangements. Neither a provider directory listing nor a recommendation establishes acceptance into every degree.

Can I use courses, training or exams I already completed?

Yes—include prior college courses, older exam results, selected workplace training, military learning and eligible certificates in your course collection. Keep original records and dates. A credential’s current recommendation does not establish the same award for every version, and military learning still receives an individual school evaluation.

Compare what those records can fill before buying more learning. Equivalent courses or overlapping certificate content must not earn duplicate degree credit. You can start a provisional plan without transcripts and refine it with the actual records later.

How do I compare the actual price and time?

Compare the whole course basket: subscription months, individual course charges, exams, proctoring, labs, books, records and required university work. A missing price must not appear as free. Allow time for assignments, grading and prerequisites; several courses can share a subscription, while a delay can add another paid month.

A partner list is a starting point for research. Sophia’s finder, for example, distinguishes partner schools from institutions sent transcripts for review. Your useful outcome is a course-by-course plan for the degree you want. Open a plan, choose the supported options that fit you, and use its next-step checklist before committing to a purchase.

About this research

DegreeSteps editorial team · Degree planning and transfer-credit research

We explain educational choices using university catalogs, receiving-school course agreements, provider guidance, and the same researched degree models used by DegreeSteps. Our articles distinguish proposed coursework, original learning records, and individual university awards. Worked examples identify their program, format, units, and relevant dates. Founder stories are attributed as reported experience, without invented transcripts, savings totals, or reviewer credentials.
